intro: Every question here is counting: how many ways can something be done? Two questions settle the method: **does order matter** (arranging) or not (selecting), and **is there a rule** (fixed places, together, at least, always included)?
There are nine short lessons: six on arranging, three on selecting. Go in order the first time.

**What the papers ask.** Two IBPS Clerk papers in the sample had one question each: 2017 (model; a committee with one person always included) and 2018 (arranging MANAGEMENT). None of the 2019 to 2025 Clerk papers checked, and none of the 12 sister papers (2025-26), had one. So this topic is light insurance for Clerk Prelims.
Practice questions are from the Guidely bank; every answer used was re-computed by script. One Guidely set (letters with repetition) has impossible answers and is not used.
after: That is the whole topic. The **Quick revision** tab has the rules on one page.
Probability builds directly on this: the number of favourable selections divided by the number of all selections.

lessons.title: Counting choices: multiply
lessons.plain: The starting point: when you make one choice and then another, multiply the numbers of ways.
teach: If a code has a first digit with 9 possible values and a second digit with 5, there are **9 x 5 = 45** codes. Each first choice can go with every second choice.
Work **place by place**, starting with the place that has a rule:
- A number cannot start with 0.
- "Divisible by 5" fixes the last digit (0 or 5).
- "No digit repeated" means each later place has one fewer choice.
- "Repetition allowed" means every place has the full set.
**Or** adds: numbers starting with 8 *or* 9 = the ones starting with 8 + the ones starting with 9.

example.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be made from 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 with no digit repeated, if the number must be even?
steps: The last digit has a rule: 2, 4 or 8, so 3 choices.
Then the first digit: 4 left; the middle: 3 left.

check.q: How many 3-digit numbers can be formed from 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 if digits may repeat?
check.why: 5 x 5 x 5 = 125. (60 forbids repeats, which the question allows.)

tags: Divisible by 5 fixes the last digit.

lessons.title: Arranging everything, and repeated letters
lessons.plain: New: all the items are arranged in a row. Some letters may repeat.
teach: n different things in a row can be arranged in **n! = n x (n - 1) x ... x 1** ways. 5! = 120, 6! = 720, 7! = 5,040, 8! = 40,320.
**Repeated letters.** Swapping two identical letters makes no new word, so divide by the factorial of each repeat count.
| Word | Letters | Arrangements |
| ARMOUR | 6, with R twice | 6! / 2! = 360 |
| TELEPHONE | 9, with E three times | 9! / 3! = 60,480 |
| MANAGEMENT | 10, with M, A, N, E each twice | 10! / (2! x 2! x 2! x 2!) = 226,800 |
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2018 asked MANAGEMENT.

example.q: In how many ways can the letters of BANANA be arranged?
steps: 6 letters: A three times, N twice.

check.q: In how many ways can the letters of LETTER be arranged?
check.why: 6 letters, E twice and T twice: 720 / 4 = 180. (360 divides by only one repeat.)

lessons.title: Arranging only some of them
lessons.plain: New: only r of the n letters are used, as in "how many 4-letter words".
teach: Choosing and arranging r of n different things: **n x (n - 1) x ... (r factors)**, written nPr.
4-letter words from the 10 different letters of LOGARITHMS: 10 x 9 x 8 x 7 = 5,040.
Check the word has no repeated letters first; this rule assumes all are different.

example.q: How many 3-letter words can be formed from the letters of NUMBER?

check.q: How many 2-letter words can be formed from the letters of PLANET?
check.why: 6 x 5 = 30. (15 counts AB and BA as the same; words are ordered.)

lessons.title: Some places are fixed
lessons.plain: New: a letter must start, end or sit in the middle.
teach: Put the fixed letters in their places first; then arrange **what is left** in the free places.
Words from COUNTRY starting with C and ending with Y: the middle 5 letters arrange in 5! = 120 ways.
Remember repeats among the letters that are left: SUMMER beginning with U leaves S, M, M, E, R: 5! / 2! = 60.

example.q: How many arrangements of PLANET begin with P and end with T?
steps: P and T are fixed. L, A, N, E fill the middle.

check.q: How many arrangements of MOTHER end with R?
check.why: R is fixed last; M, O, T, H, E arrange in 5! = 120. (720 ignores the rule.)

tags: Fixed first, with a repeat left.

lessons.title: Keeping some together
lessons.plain: New: certain letters or people must sit side by side.
teach: **Tie the group into one block.** Arrange the block with the others, then arrange the members inside the block, and multiply.
SIMPLE with the vowels I, E together: block + S, M, P, L = 5 units: 5! = 120; inside the block 2! = 2; total 240.
**Two groups each together** (all boys together and all girls together): 2 ways to order the two blocks x arrangements inside each.
Divide for repeats inside and outside the block as usual.

example.q: 4 boys and 3 girls sit in a row with all the girls together. In how many ways?

check.q: In how many ways can the letters of FATHER be arranged with the vowels together?
check.why: Vowels A, E as one block + F, T, H, R = 5 units: 120 x 2 = 240. (120 forgets the order inside the block.)

tags: Repeats inside and outside the block.
Three vowels together, a repeat outside.

lessons.title: Apart, alternate, and round a table
teach: **Never all together** = all arrangements - arrangements with them together.
**Alternate** (boys and girls take turns in a row of 5 + 5): start with a boy or a girl (2 ways) x 5! x 5!.
**Round a table:** fix one person to remove the rotations; n people make (n - 1)! arrangements.
Two particular people **not** side by side round a table: (n - 1)! - 2 x (n - 2)!.

example.q: 6 people sit round a table. In how many ways?
steps: Fix one person; arrange the other 5.

check.q: 4 boys and 4 girls sit in a row, boys and girls alternating. In how many ways?
check.why: 2 starts x 4! x 4! = 2 x 24 x 24 = 1,152. (576 forgets that a girl may start.)

lessons.title: Selecting, when order does not matter
lessons.plain: New: a team or committee. Choosing A then B is the same team as B then A.
teach: Choosing r from n when order does not matter: **nCr = nPr / r!**. 6C4 = (6 x 5 x 4 x 3) / (4 x 3 x 2 x 1) = 15.
Shortcut: nCr = nC(n - r). 8C6 = 8C2 = 28.
Choosing from two groups at once: multiply. 4 men from 6 **and** 3 women from 5: 6C4 x 5C3 = 15 x 10 = 150.
Is it arranging or selecting? A **word, number, seating or ranking** is arranging (order matters). A **team, group, committee or handful** is selecting.

example.q: In how many ways can 3 men and 2 women be chosen from 5 men and 4 women?

check.q: In how many ways can a team of 3 be chosen from 7 players?
check.why: 7C3 = (7 x 6 x 5) / 6 = 35. (210 is 7P3, which treats the order as different.)

lessons.title: At least and at most
lessons.plain: New: the team must contain at least (or at most) so many of a kind.
teach: List the cases and add them. At least 3 men in 5 from 6 men and 7 women: (3 men, 2 women) + (4, 1) + (5, 0).
**At least one** is quickest the other way round: all selections - selections with none of them.
At least one of each: all - (all of the first kind) - (all of the second kind).
Checked papers: IBPS Clerk 2017 (model) set a committee with a condition.

example.q: A committee of 4 is chosen from 7 men and 8 women, and one particular woman must be included. How many committees are possible?
steps: She is in; choose the other 3 from the remaining 14 people.

check.q: From 5 boys and 4 girls, 3 are chosen. How many selections have at least one girl?
check.why: All 9C3 = 84, minus all-boy 5C3 = 10: 74. (84 forgets to remove the all-boy teams.)

tags: At least one: all minus none.
At least three: add the cases.
At least one of each kind.

lessons.title: Someone always in, someone always out
lessons.plain: New: particular people must be included or left out.
teach: **Always included:** put them in and choose the rest from the others. **Always excluded:** remove them from the pool.
A team of 9 from 16 with 2 always out and 1 always in: pool 16 - 2 - 1 = 13, places left 9 - 1 = 8: 13C8 = 1,287.

example.q: A committee of 5 is chosen from 12 people, with 2 particular people always included. How many committees?
steps: Both are in; choose 3 more from the other 10.

check.q: A team of 4 is chosen from 10 players, with one particular player always left out. How many teams?
check.why: Choose all 4 from the other 9: 9C4 = 126. (84 is 9C3, which also drops a place.)

pemutation-and-combination-based-on-sele: 8 boys and 7 girls: choose one of each.
permutation-and-combination-based-on-num: First digit: 1 to 9, so 9 choices. Second: an odd digit, 5 choices.
The last digit must be 5. The first and middle come from the other 4 digits without repeats.
Digits 0 to 6. The first place cannot be 0: 6 choices.
The first digit is 8 or 9: 2 choices.
Then 7 and 6 choices from the remaining digits.
permutation-and-combination-based-on-let: MANAGEMENT: 10 letters; M, A, N and E each twice.
permutation-and-combination-based-on-end: C first and Y last; O, U, N, T, R in between.
R last; N, O, M, A, L before it.
B first; F, E, R, U, A, R, Y remain, with R twice.
U first; S, M, M, E, R remain, with M twice.
T first and E in the 4th place; P, N, A, L, Y fill the other 5 places.
pemutation-and-combination-based-on-word: Vowels I, E as one block + S, M, P, L: 5 units, 5! = 120.
Vowels E, I, E as one block + S, R, S: 4 units with S twice: 4! / 2! = 12.
Vowels O, I, A as one block + L, G, C, L: 5 units with L twice: 5! / 2! = 60.
permutation-and-combination-based-on-sit: The two women as one block + 3 men = 4 units: 4! = 24.
Boys' block and girls' block: 2 orders.
Start with a girl or a boy: 2 ways.
pemutation-and-combination-based-on-pers: All round-table arrangements: 9!. With the two together: 2 x 8!.
pemutation-and-combination-based-on-word: TELEVISION: 10 letters, E twice and I twice: 10! / 4 = 907,200 arrangements.
Vowels E, E, I, I, O as one block: 6! x (5! / 4) = 720 x 30 = 21,600.
pemutation-and-combination-based-on-atle: All outcomes 6 x 6 x 6 = 216. No 3 at all: 5 x 5 x 5 = 125.
permutation-and-combination-based-on-inc: She is in; choose 4 more from the other 10.
